reference.title: Benign, HGPIN, ASAP and adenocarcinoma
reference.intro: Carcinoma needs the architecture, the cytology and the absent basal cell layer together. Where a small focus is suspicious but falls short, ASAP is the honest answer.

groups.heading: Benign
points: Glands are lobular, with papillary infoldings and undulating luminal borders
A basal cell layer is present, patchy on H&E and continuous on p63 / 34betaE12
Nuclei are small and uniform; nucleoli are inconspicuous
Corpora amylacea are common; crystalloids are not

images.caption: Normal prostatic glands: undulating luminal borders, pale cytoplasm and a basal cell layer
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Hyperplastic gland with pale to clear cytoplasm matching the adjacent benign acini (x200)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 1c (cropped)

groups.heading: HGPIN
points: Pre-existing large glands lined by crowded, stratified cells with enlarged nuclei and prominent nucleoli
Tufting, micropapillary or flat growth; the gland keeps its native size and contour
Basal cells remain, though they may be discontinuous
Distinguish from: IDC-P (duct expansion, dense cribriform or solid growth, necrosis, marked pleomorphism)

images.caption: High grade PIN: enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei with nucleoli in a pre-existing gland
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Tufted HGPIN with pseudostratified columnar cells, nucleomegaly, hyperchromasia and nucleoli (200x)
images.credit: Smith & Wobker, Cancers 2024, Fig 1A (cropped)

images.caption: Flat HGPIN: lower cuboidal atypical epithelium, a pattern that can simulate invasive carcinoma (400x)
images.credit: Smith & Wobker, Cancers 2024, Fig 1C (cropped)

images.caption: HGPIN immunophenotype: retained p63/HMWCK basal cells (brown) with AMACR overexpression (red) (100x)
images.credit: Smith & Wobker, Cancers 2024, Fig 2B (cropped)

groups.heading: ASAP
points: A small focus of crowded glands, atypical but too few, too distorted or too poorly preserved to be called carcinoma
Basal cell stain equivocal, negative in a focus too small to trust, or lost on the recut
Descriptive alternative: 'atypical glands suspicious for but not diagnostic of adenocarcinoma'
Do not assign a Gleason score to ASAP

images.caption: Atypical small acinar proliferation: a small focus of crowded atypical glands at the edge of the core
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: The same focus at higher power: too few glands and too little atypia to call carcinoma outright
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Adenocarcinoma
points: Infiltrative small glands between benign glands, or any of the pattern 4 / 5 architectures
Enlarged nuclei with prominent nucleoli, amphophilic cytoplasm and a sharp luminal border
No basal cells on p63 / 34betaE12; AMACR is usually positive but does not stand alone
Supporting features: perineural invasion, mucinous fibroplasia, glomerulations, intraluminal crystalloids, blue mucin

images.caption: Acinar adenocarcinoma: discrete infiltrating glands lacking a basal cell layer (Gleason score 3+3=6)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2a

images.caption: Double and marginated nucleoli in acinar adenocarcinoma (arrows) (H&E, 400x)
images.credit: Cruz et al., J Bras Patol Med Lab 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, panel D (cropped)

images.caption: Intraluminal crystalloid: an eosinophilic, sharply angulated luminal crystal
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Circumferential perineural invasion by adenocarcinoma
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Benign mimics of carcinoma
points: Adenosis (atypical adenomatous hyperplasia): a lobular cluster of small glands with pale cytoplasm and patchy basal cells
Partial atrophy: crowded pale glands with scant cytoplasm, nuclei reaching the luminal surface, basal cells retained
Seminal vesicle / ejaculatory duct: lipofuscin pigment, marked degenerative nuclear atypia without mitoses
Cowper glands: lobules of bland mucinous acini beside skeletal muscle
Nephrogenic adenoma: small tubules with hobnail cells and basement membrane thickening, PAX8 positive
Basal cell hyperplasia: solid or cribriform nests of basal cells, p63 positive throughout

images.caption: Adenosis: a circumscribed lobular cluster of small glands merging with larger benign glands
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Atrophy: small angulated glands lined by attenuated cells with scant cytoplasm
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Seminal vesicle epithelium: degenerative nuclear atypia with golden lipofuscin pigment
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Cowper (bulbourethral) glands: lobules of bland mucinous acini
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Nephrogenic adenoma: small tubules with hobnail cells and a hyaline rim
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Basal cell hyperplasia: small solid and glandular nests of uniform basal cells
images.credit: Librepath, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

reference.title: Gleason patterns 3, 4 and 5
reference.intro: Grade what is present at the 10x objective. Pattern 3 keeps individual glands; pattern 4 loses either the separate wall (fused, cribriform) or the lumen (poorly formed); pattern 5 abandons gland formation altogether.

groups.heading: Pattern 3 - discrete, separate glands
points: Individual glands are well formed and separate, each surrounded by stroma, however small or crowded
Gland size varies; small, branching and atrophic-looking glands are still pattern 3
Every lumen is circumscribed by a single layer of tumour cells with no shared walls
Distinguish from: pattern 4, where glands lose their individual walls (fused) or lumina (poorly formed)

images.caption: Gleason score 3+3=6: discrete, separate, variably sized glands, each with its own lumen
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2a

images.caption: Discrete pattern 3 glands encircling a nerve (circumferential perineural invasion)
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Small separate acini with blue-tinged luminal mucin (arrow) (H&E, 200x)
images.credit: Cruz et al., J Bras Patol Med Lab 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, panel A (cropped)

groups.heading: Pattern 4 - poorly formed, fused, cribriform or glomeruloid
points: Poorly formed glands: cell clusters with no lumen or only an abortive one, more than an occasional focus, recognisable at the 10x objective
Fused glands: chains or nests in which adjacent glands share walls and the stroma between them is lost
Cribriform glands: a confluent sheet of tumour cells punched by multiple lumina, no intervening stroma or mucin
Glomeruloid glands: an intraluminal cribriform tuft attached to the gland wall at one point, like a renal glomerulus
Cribriform and glomeruloid growth are pattern 4 whatever their size or number

images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2d

images.caption: Glomeruloid glands: intraluminal cribriform tufts attached at one edge (Gleason score 4+4=8)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2e

images.caption: Irregular cribriform glands (Gleason score 4+4=8)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2c

images.caption: Gleason score 3+4=7: discrete pattern 3 glands with a minor cribriform component
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2b

images.caption: Pattern 4 across a needle core at low power
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Pattern 4: crowded, poorly delimited and partly fused glands
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Pattern 5 - sheets, cords, single cells, comedonecrosis
points: Solid sheets, nests or cylinders of tumour with no gland formation
Single cells and single-file cords infiltrating stroma
Solid nests pierced by rosette-like spaces still count as pattern 5, not cribriform pattern 4
Unequivocal comedonecrosis within solid or cribriform masses is pattern 5, even when focal
Distinguish from: crushed or cauterised pattern 3, inflammation and lymphocytes, and the granular cells of xanthoma or histiocytes

images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3a

images.caption: Cords of tumour cells (Gleason score 5+5=10)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3b

images.caption: Individually infiltrating tumour cells (Gleason score 5+5=10)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3c

images.caption: Cribriform glands, some with central comedonecrosis (Gleason score 4+5=9)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3d

images.caption: Pattern 5 sheets and single cells adjacent to a pattern 4 component
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Borderline 3 vs 4 - favour the lower grade
points: Occasional poorly formed or fused glands among well-formed glands are not enough for pattern 4
Tangential sections through the edge of well-formed glands produce apparent poorly formed glands; look at the neighbouring planes
Crush artefact and thick sections both fabricate fusion; where morphology is borderline or crushed, grade the lower pattern
Distinguish from: adenosis (atypical adenomatous hyperplasia) and partial atrophy, which are benign crowded small glands with at least patchy basal cells

images.caption: Bordering 3+3=6 with tangential cuts against 3+4=7 with poorly formed glands; the ISUP panel favoured 3+3=6 (H&E, x20 objective)
images.credit: Egevad et al., Virchows Arch 2020, Fig 3a (cropped)

images.caption: Same differential with more convincingly fused glands; the panel favoured 3+4=7 (H&E, x20 objective)
images.credit: Egevad et al., Virchows Arch 2020, Fig 3c (cropped)

images.caption: Bordering 3+4=7 against 4+3=7 (H&E, x20 objective)
images.credit: Egevad et al., Virchows Arch 2020, Fig 4a (cropped)

images.caption: Mostly cribriform and glomeruloid glands with occasional separate glands: bordering 4+3=7 against 4+4=8 (H&E, x20 objective)
images.credit: Egevad et al., Virchows Arch 2020, Fig 4d (cropped)

images.caption: Mimic: atrophic benign glands are small and angulated but retain a basal layer and lack nucleolar atypia
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Mimic: adenosis, a crowded lobular proliferation of small bland glands
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

reference.noteTop: Grade Group 1 = 3+3; 2 = 3+4; 3 = 4+3; 4 = score 8 (4+4, 3+5, 5+3); 5 = score 9-10. On needle biopsy the highest pattern is included in the score whatever its extent; the 5% rule applies only to radical prostatectomy.

reference.title: Minor (tertiary) pattern 5
reference.intro: The 2019 ISUP consensus prefers 'minor' to 'tertiary'. On needle biopsy a minor high-grade pattern is not a tertiary grade: it is taken into the score as the secondary pattern whatever its extent.

groups.heading: Minor pattern 5 on needle biopsy
points: A small focus of sheets, cords, single cells or comedonecrosis against a background of pattern 3 or 4
On biopsy it enters the score: 60% pattern 4, 36% pattern 3, 4% pattern 5 is reported as 4+5 = 9, Grade Group 5
Record it so that a patient is not offered active surveillance on the strength of the majority pattern

images.caption: A small pattern 5 component (sheets and single cells) beside pattern 4 glands
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Predominantly cribriform tumour with an area of seemingly dispersed cells and strands; crush artefact was considered and the panel split between 4+4=8 and 9 (H&E, x20 objective)
images.credit: Egevad et al., Virchows Arch 2020, Fig 5b (cropped)

groups.heading: Pattern 5 as a true secondary grade
points: Pattern 5 is the second most common pattern by area, not a minor focus
Score directly as 3+5 = 8 or 4+5 = 9; no separate minor-pattern statement is needed

images.caption: Pale cells forming gland-like nests together with strands and single cells (H&E, x20 objective)
images.credit: Egevad et al., Virchows Arch 2020, Fig 5c (cropped)

images.caption: Poorly formed, tapered tadpole-like structures merging into strands (H&E, x20 objective)
images.credit: Egevad et al., Virchows Arch 2020, Fig 5d (cropped)

images.caption: Comedonecrosis within cribriform glands, sufficient on its own for pattern 5 (Gleason score 4+5=9)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3d

images.caption: Solid sheets: pattern 5 as a secondary grade when it sits beside pattern 4
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3a

groups.heading: The 5% rule (resections only)
points: In a radical prostatectomy the highest pattern must reach 5% of the tumour to be taken as the secondary grade
Below 5% the score uses the primary and secondary patterns and the minor pattern is given in a comment
60% pattern 3, 37% pattern 4, 3% pattern 5 is 3+4 = 7 with minor pattern 5; 60% / 30% / 10% is 3+5 = 8

reference.note: Do not apply the 5% rule to a needle biopsy.

fields.label: Percentage of pattern 4/5
fields.help: Recorded when pattern 4 or 5 is present. Leave blank for 3+3 or 5+5.

reference.title: Cribriform pattern 4
reference.intro: Cribriform growth carries a worse outcome than poorly formed or fused pattern 4, so it is stated separately in Gleason score 7 and 8 cancers. Where basal cell stains are not available, 'cribriform glands present' covers both invasive cribriform carcinoma and IDC-P.

groups.heading: Cribriform: the ISUP definition
points: A confluent sheet of contiguous tumour cells with multiple lumina, easily seen at the 10x objective
No stroma and no mucin separating the individual or fused glandular structures
Transluminal bridging with a dense cell mass filling at least half the lumen
Most of the cells inside the gland are out of contact with stroma

images.caption: Confluent sheets of tumour cells forming cohesive trabeculae with punched-out lumina and no intervening stroma (H&E, 100x)
images.credit: Compérat et al., Cancers 2024, Fig 2

images.caption: Irregular cribriform glands (Gleason score 4+4=8)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2c

groups.heading: Large vs small cribriform
points: Large cribriform glands are the ones with the consistent adverse outcome data
Thresholds in use: diameter at least twice an adjacent benign gland, or above 0.25 mm, or more than twelve lumina
No threshold is adopted by WHO; report cribriform growth as present rather than sizing it in the report

images.caption: Large, complex cribriform structure invading periprostatic adipose tissue (x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 4b (cropped)

images.caption: A small cribriform focus arising among discrete pattern 3 glands (Gleason score 3+4=7)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2b

groups.heading: Not cribriform
points: Glomeruloid glands: the tuft is attached to the gland wall at a single point (still pattern 4)
Fused glands where stroma or vessels still run between the lumina
Mucinous fibroplasia (collagenous micronodules), where the bridging is by stroma and mucin
Partial bridging only, or a clear peripheral luminal space around more than half the circumference

images.caption: Glomeruloid glands: the intraluminal tuft stays attached at one edge, so this is not cribriform
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2e

images.caption: Benign glands with luminal tufting and pseudostratification producing a cribriform-like pattern; basal cells retained and no atypia (x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 1a (cropped)

images.caption: Basal cell hyperplasia with a cribriform pattern (x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 1b (cropped)

images.caption: Clear cell cribriform hyperplasia with bland monotonous nuclei (x200)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 1d (cropped)

reference.title: Intraductal carcinoma of the prostate
reference.intro: IDC-P is a malignant proliferation filling and expanding pre-existing ducts and acini, with basal cells retained. It is not given a Gleason grade of its own; when it stands alone in a biopsy, grade nothing and say so.

groups.heading: IDC-P: essential criteria
points: An expansile proliferation within the pre-existing duct-acinar system, the ducts usually distended well beyond neighbouring benign glands
Lumen-spanning solid, dense cribriform or comedo growth, or loose cribriform / micropapillary growth with enlarged pleomorphic nuclei
Residual basal cells, at least in part, shown by p63 or 34betaE12 where the distinction changes the report
Almost always beside high-grade invasive carcinoma; IDC-P alone occurs in well under 1% of biopsies

images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 3a (cropped)

images.caption: Confluent intraductal proliferation occupying the duct lumen (H&E, x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 3b (cropped)

images.caption: 34betaE12 highlights the retained peripheral basal cell layer (x100)

groups.heading: IDC-P vs invasive cribriform carcinoma
points: Invasive cribriform carcinoma has no basal cells; IDC-P retains at least a partial layer
The distinction is not reliable on H&E: an apparently invasive cribriform or comedonecrotic focus may prove intraductal on staining
When the invasive component is graded, an associated cribriform focus is pattern 4 and a solid or comedonecrotic one is pattern 5

groups.heading: IDC-P vs high grade PIN
points: HGPIN keeps the architecture of the native gland: tufting, micropapillary, flat or loose cribriform growth without duct expansion
IDC-P shows atypia beyond HGPIN - marked nuclear enlargement and pleomorphism, dense cribriform or solid growth, or necrosis
Cribriform HGPIN is no longer recognised as an entity; a cribriform intraductal proliferation is reported as IDC-P or as atypical
The 'nuclei six times benign' rule has been dropped from WHO; read it as markedly enlarged and pleomorphic
